decision: Shortlist trades by dollars earned from plausible wing normalization versus adverse-path losses, not highest z-score.
key_points: Pandar described recurring expansion/collapse, an unusually overpriced expiry, and survivable sizing; numerical mean-reversion rules are our proposed research.
Separate broad call slope, local strike residual, and term dislocation. MRVL's rich wing does not establish a local kink: neighboring mid-IVs rise smoothly.
Hold ATM, spot and time fixed; partially normalize only the wing and fully reprice. Subtract executable round-trip costs. Separately stress rallies, wing widening and overnight gaps.
Reprice both legs together. A higher-strike long caps the short call; a lower-strike long converts it into bullish exposure. Their economics and purpose differ.
Keep nondominated choices across normalization dollars, stress loss, liquidity and time exposure; delta and distance describe risk rather than impose universal cutoffs.

Estimate normalization frequency and speed from prior comparable episodes, including persistent and widening wings. Condition simply on episode age and expansion versus rollover; sparse evidence stays uncertain. HIRO helps time observable flow changes, not establish dealer gamma sign.
risks: Verify kinks against synchronized bid/ask envelopes and neighboring quotes. My prohibition on naked convexity is my persona's risk preference; Pandar explicitly sold naked calls.
confidence: High on mechanics; unproven predictive edge.
